title: A photo from another day, logged under a meal of today, leaves two dinners on its day
short: A meal is logged on one day, at the meal's time, picked in one edit mode
rel: Proposed; not agreed until Coach Milan says Go
boardTitle: B150: a photo from another day, logged under a meal of today, leaves two dinners on its day

opportunity.from: Coach Milan, 18 November 2026, 19:21, with a screenshot of his Plan on Tuesday 17 November. Found while testing the last releases on his phone.
opportunity.job: Log a photo of a meal I ate on another day, to that day and that meal.
opportunity.kind: A wrong record, on two days at once. The day I ate it shows two dinners. Today's dinner counts as eaten though I have not had it.
opportunity.why_now: It is in the releases under test, and every photo picked from Your photos can end this way.

problem: I read a photo from Tuesday 19:56. I tried it as today's lunch first, then wanted its real time. The pencil's calendar showed a dinner at 18:00 and I took it. Now Tuesday shows Chicken and sweet potato fries as Dinner, 19:56, and under it the planned dinner, Chicken rice bowl, still asks I ate it, I skipped it.
story: When I log a photo from another day, I want it to land on one day, as the meal I picked, so that the day shows what I ate once and no planned meal keeps asking.
words: 18 November 19:21: the dinner around that timing was only possible for the time slot as planned in the calendar at 18h. And now we have two dinners. One as set from the read, and the one planned in the list.
cause: Two things together. The pencil's calendar opens on today, also for a photo from another day, so the Dinner you tapped was Wednesday's dinner. The meal was then logged with the photo's own time, Tuesday 19:56. One record held Tuesday's time and Wednesday's dinner. Tuesday lists it by its time; Tuesday's planned dinner is closed only by a Tuesday dinner, so it still asks.
proposed: One status and one edit mode. With no meal picked the line says Just looking, and nothing is counted. The pencil opens edit mode and turns into the X that closes it. Edit mode is the calendar you know: it opens on the photo's day, with the photo's time as a reference that cannot be changed. A tap on a meal picks it, saved at once, no Done. The time in the picked meal's row is a field: the meal's time in the calendar, for this meal on this day. A tap on Just looking takes the meal off again. And one rule where a meal is logged: its day is the day of the meal I picked, its time is that meal's time in the calendar.
repair: The record from Tuesday is still wrong on your phone. Proposed: when the app opens, a record whose meal is on a later day than its own time is moved to the meal of its own day. Yours becomes Tuesday's dinner; Wednesday's dinner opens again.

ac.title: No meal picked is Just looking
ac.text: Given a photo is read and I picked no meal, when I look at the meal line, then it says Just looking, Not counted, with the pencil, and the read ends with What do you do with it?.

ac.title: The pencil opens edit mode, the X closes it
ac.text: Given that read of a photo from Saturday 15:57, when I tap the pencil, then edit mode opens on Sat 14 with Just looking marked, the pencil is an X, and a tap on the X closes edit mode.

ac.title: The photo's time is a reference
ac.text: Given edit mode for that photo, when I look above the days, then one line says The photo was taken on Saturday, 15:57, and a tap on it does nothing.

ac.title: A meal is picked and saved at once
ac.text: Given edit mode is open, when I tap Dinner, then Dinner is marked, the line says Dinner, Saturday, 14 November, 20:00 at once, edit mode stays open, and there is no Done.

ac.title: I change the meal's time in the calendar
ac.text: Given Dinner is marked, when I tap the time in its row and set 19:30, then the line says Dinner, Saturday, 14 November, 19:30.

ac.title: Only this meal, only this day
ac.text: Given I set Saturday's dinner to 19:30, when I open Slots and times or another day, then Dinner is at 20:00 there.

ac.title: Closed, the line keeps the meal and the pencil
ac.text: Given Dinner at 19:30 is picked, when I tap the X, then the line shows Dinner, Saturday, 14 November, 19:30 with the pencil, and the read asks Did you eat it?.

ac.title: One dinner on the photo's day
ac.text: Given that read and a Chicken rice bowl planned for Saturday's dinner, when I choose All of it and tap Done, then Saturday shows my meal as Dinner, 19:30, the Chicken rice bowl no longer asks, and today shows nothing of it.

ac.title: Back to Just looking
ac.text: Given Dinner is picked, when I open edit mode and tap Just looking, then the line says Just looking, Not counted, and the read ends with What do you do with it? again.

ac.title: A meal of today, when I mean today
ac.text: Given edit mode on Sat 14, when I tap Sun 15, today and then Dinner, then the line says Dinner, Sunday, 15 November, and after All of it and Done the meal is today's dinner and Saturday shows nothing of it.

ac.title: One day per record
ac.text: Given a meal is logged from a photo by any way (the read, the plate, Ate it, edit mode), when I open the Plan, then it shows on the day of the meal I picked and on no other day.

ac.title: The record on your phone
ac.text: Given a record with the time Tuesday 19:56 and the dinner of Wednesday, when the app opens after the release, then it is Tuesday's dinner, Tuesday's planned dinner no longer asks, and Wednesday's dinner is open again.

ac.title: A plate without a photo
ac.text: Given a plate I built with no photo, when I open edit mode, then it opens on today with no line about a photo, and everything else is the same.

unchanged: The photo screen and the read, but for the meal line.
What do you do with it? Save it, Plan it, Ate it, and Ate it's calendar.
Did you eat it?, All of it, Half, Part of it, Done.
The days and the rows of the calendar, and What is it? and the kind of moment under it.
Slots and times in the settings.
A dinner logged after midnight stays with the evening before.
details: No new screen. The meal line, the calendar and its Just looking row are the ones you know.
One new thing in the calendar: the time in the picked meal's row is a field. One new line: the photo's time as a reference.
The rule sits in the one place a meal is logged, so every way obeys it. The repair touches only records whose meal is on a later day than their time.
The row B150.1 on this board, steps 1 to 6 and Back to Just looking, is what it looks like.
words2: 18 November 19:34: I couldn't change the timing; it was only the timing from the settings. 19:43: better an edit mode where what is needed is set, than another way of correction. 19:49: edit mode is when the pencil is clicked and turns into an X to close it; saved automatically, no Done. The time of the picture is a reference; what should be changed is the timing in the calendar. 20:12: the X was to remove the meal and the pencil to edit, so there is no proper solution for no meal selected. Maybe the default is the status Just looking, or select the meal. Without selection it is not counted. When selected, the meal with its timing is displayed. What we need is the way from a selected meal back to Just looking. And: draw the new flow whole, with the existing screens, and say which did not change.
time_now: Once a meal is set, the pencil is gone. An X stands in its place, and it does not close anything: it takes the meal off. The line says Dinner, Saturday, 14 November, 20:00. The time is words, so it cannot be changed.
time_proposed: One icon, one edit mode. The line always has the pencil. A tap opens edit mode and the pencil turns into the X that closes it. Every change is saved at once; there is no Done. In edit mode: the photo's time as one line of reference, which cannot be changed; the days; the meals. The time in the marked meal's row is a field: a tap opens the phone's clock and sets the meal's time, for this meal on this day only.
more_change: Three things change that 0.3.157 built, so you see them before a Go. 1. Meal and day not set becomes Just looking. Today these are two states; they become one, and it does what no meal set does today: the page ends with What do you do with it?. 2. The X that removed the meal goes. The icon is the pencil, then the X that closes; Just looking in edit mode removes the meal. 3. A photo logged to a meal is logged at the meal's time in the calendar. Today a photo of that same day is logged at the photo's time.
days: The board is drawn on the app's test days. The photo is from Saturday 15:57: that is your Tuesday 19:56. Today is Sunday: that is your Wednesday.
